stories.title: 3 Italian ‘Hobbits’ Searched for Irishman’s ‘Precious’ Wedding Ring for Days Before Bringing it to His Home
stories.label: people
stories.summary: An Irish tourist lost his wedding ring in a mountain stream while on vacation in Italy, and thought it was gone for good. Three young local men, inspired by the loyalty and determination of Tolkien's hobbits, spent days searching the stream until they found it. Rather than keep it or sell it, they tracked down the man's address and delivered the ring to his home themselves. It's a small, sweet reminder that strangers still go out of their way to do the right thing for no reward at all. The Irishman got his precious back, and three new friends in Italy besides.
stories.why_good: A real act of kindness that actually happened, with no political angle and no suffering at its core - just strangers choosing generosity.

stories.title: New U.S. National Park Preserves 'Land of Standing-Up Rocks' and its Apache Culture in Arizona
stories.label: earth
stories.summary: Arizona's striking rock-spire landscape, long known as Chiricahua, has officially been upgraded from a national monument to a full national park. The area holds deep meaning for the Apache people, and the new designation honors that heritage while giving the stunning natural formations stronger long-term protection. It's a place full of towering stone pillars that look almost otherworldly, and now more people will discover it and its history. The change also typically brings more resources for preserving the land for future generations.
stories.why_good: A real, finalized land designation that protects a unique natural and cultural site, with no political fight involved.

stories.title: Minnesota Man Jumps Onto Runaway School Bus and Saves 18 Kids After Driver Has Seizure
stories.label: people
stories.summary: On a quiet Monday in St. Paul, Minnesota, a 27-year-old man named Ebro Ahmed was on a break from work when he saw a school bus rolling by with no one in control. Without hesitating, he ran alongside it, pulled himself aboard, and brought the bus safely to a stop. It turned out the driver had suffered a sudden seizure, but thanks to Ebro's quick thinking, all 18 children on board and the driver were kept completely safe. No one was hurt, and a split-second decision by an ordinary guy turned a scary moment into a story of everyday heroism.
stories.why_good: A real, completed act of courage that prevented a disaster before it happened, with everyone safe and no political angle at all.
